Yes, but selectively. On Linux, Ghostty uses GTK4 + libadwaita, and it reads a limited set of system values:

**What it does read:**
- **Dark/light mode** — via `AdwStyleManager` (libadwaita), which itself reads `org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme` from GSettings. On KDE or non-GNOME desktops this requires the XDG Desktop Portal (or `ADW_DISABLE_PORTAL=1` as a workaround).
- **Display scaling / DPI** — picks up text and display scale factors from the desktop environment automatically.
- **Window decorations** — uses server-side decorations (CSD vs SSD) based on the compositor/GTK negotiation.

**What it does NOT read:**
- System GTK font (`gtk-font-name`) — you set fonts explicitly in `~/.config/ghostty/config`.
- GTK color theme (e.g., Adwaita colors, custom GTK themes) — Ghostty manages its own palette entirely.
- `gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme` — this is unsupported with libadwaita; `AdwStyleManager:color-scheme` is used instead.

In short: Ghostty reads the system dark/light preference and DPI through GTK/libadwaita/portal plumbing, but ignores the GTK theme itself — fonts and colors are Ghostty-native config.

- [Ghostty Config Reference](https://ghostty.org/docs/config/reference)
- [Light theme regression on KDE · ghostty-org/ghostty #8245](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/issues/8245)
